basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Vixitque Sem postquam genuit Arfaxat quingentos annos, et genuit filios et filias.'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Vixitque Sem postquam genuit Arfaxat quingentos annos, et genuit filios et filias. Nusquam in tota hac serie generationum additur, sicut in ea quae diluvium praecessit aetate, et mortuus est; quia nemo erat in tota hac complexione nascentium, de quo a caeteris excepto dici posset, sicut ibi de Enoch ambulavitque cum Deo, et non apparuit, quia tulit eum Deus (Gen. V, 24).
